subtopic: Managed Relational Databases (RDS / Aurora) Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #24: A multi-region cloud deployment experienced severe traffic blackholing and split-brain DNS state in Cloud Storage, Databases & Lifecycle Policies. During an automated regional failover simulation for 'Managed Relational Databases (RDS / Aurora) Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas', cross-region database replication lagged by 18 minutes.

### Engineering Challenge:
Which cloud architecture configuration guarantees minimal Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for 'Managed Relational Databases (RDS / Aurora) Multi-AZ vs Read Replicas'?

options.text: Manually update authoritative public nameserver records at the domain registrar during outages.
Deploy synchronous two-phase commit over public internet transit across 10,000 miles.
Rely on nightly tape backups restored to a single cold server instance.
Implement Route 53 latency-based routing with health checks, Global Accelerator anycast IP failover, and asynchronous cross-region Aurora Global Database storage replication.

answer_explanation: In Cloud Storage, Databases & Lifecycle Policies, automated disaster recovery requires Anycast IP routing (AWS Global Accelerator) or DNS health-checked failover combined with storage-level replication (Aurora Global Database) to achieve RTO under 1 minute and RPO under 1 second without split-brain.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option D. Rationale: In Cloud Storage, Databases & Lifecycle Policies, automated disaster recovery requires Anycast IP routing (AWS Global Accelerator) or DNS health-checked failover combined with storage-level replication (Aurora Global Database) to achieve RTO under 1 minute and RPO under 1 second without split-brain.
